title: Percentile Traffic Scheduler: Walkthrough and Annotations
content:
Purpose / scope:
This note captures a focused UX walkthrough for a new traffic-scheduling surface we’re calling the ‘Percentile Traffic Scheduler’ — a compact operator-first flow for configuring staged releases (canary, progressive percentiles, and A/B targets) with integrated automatic fallback policies. Goal: let an operator answer the question ‘Which percent of production traffic should route to this variant at time T, and what happens if latency/error percentiles breach thresholds?’ in under 90 seconds.

Core assumptions (context):
- Backend will accept schedule entries of the form {time-offset, target-percent, model-variant-id, optional-traffic-conditions}.
- Telemetry provides p50/p90/p99 latency and error-rate signals per route-model-variant at 10s granularity.
- We have an existing policy engine capable of automatic rollback and fallback to an alternate variant or region.
- Operators are typically SREs or platform engineers; need clear safeguards and obvious audit trail.

High-level flow (operator journey):
1) Create rollout: pick base route and select variants (control + 1..N).
2) Define percent schedule: drag to add 0 -> X% -> Y% -> 100%, or pick a simple preset (canary-only, linear-48h, stepped-24h).
3) Attach guardrails: thresholds (latency p95, error-rate), evaluation window, required stability window (e.g., 5m stable before next step).
4) Configure fallback: choose automatic fallback action (switch to control, switch to a safe-model, or fall back to regional replica). Optionally add a notify channel and a human approval step.
5) Review & commit: visual timeline + estimated cost delta + expected p95 impact (calculated heuristically).
6) Monitor: live timeline with telemetry overlays + single-click abort/step-down.

Wireframe annotations (compact console card view):
- Top header: rollout name | route selector | live indicator (green/yellow/red)
- Timeline canvas (left): horizontal time axis, vertical lanes per variant showing percent wedge. Overlaid translucent telemetry ribbons (p95 latency color gradient).
- Right panel (config): small editable list: presets, manual steps, guardrails, fallback. Each step row expandable.
- Bottom: quick actions: start, pause, abort, promote (manual promote to 100%), change-schedule (mutations allowed only when not actively ramping unless you check an ‘override’ box).

Microcopy and affordances (proposal):
- Button text: Start rollout (avoid Launch) — communicates staged nature.
- Guardrail label: ‘Automatic rollback when p95 >’ (use numeric input + adaptive suggested thresholds link).
- Fallback selector: radio: [Switch to control] [Switch to safe-model] [Route to region X] [Pause traffic] — tooltip: explains latency vs data-residency tradeoffs.
- Confirm modals: require typing route name for abort-to-prevent accidental aborts on live rollouts.

Telemetry overlays — UX details:
- Use semi-transparent ribbons behind each variant wedge: green if p95 within guardrails, amber if within 25% of threshold, red if breached.
- Small per-step metric badges showing p50/p95/error for last 5m. Clicking badge expands a sparkline (10s buckets).
- Timeline scrubber: hover at a timestamp to see what percent was routed where and the metric snapshot.

Backlog grooming notes (priority ordered):
- MUST: Add ‘stability window’ enforcement in backend API; surface violation events in rollout timeline (JIRA-9876).
- MUST: Telemetry mapping: ensure metric tags include variant-id and route-id for correct aggregation (task for instrumentation team).
- SHOULD: Cost estimator: show delta tokens/compute per step using historical token-distribution on route. Low priority if backend cost API blocked.
- SHOULD: Preset editor for common patterns (linear ramp, exponential backoff).
- NICE-TO-HAVE: Simulate button that replays historical 7-day traffic and predicts expected violations given current guardrails (for operator confidence).
- UX TASK: Design microcopy for override path — explain risks and require two-step confirmation.

Edge cases and questions to resolve:
- Q: If a variant’s telemetry disappears (no reports) during a step, we should default to immediate fallback or pause? Proposal: treat as telemetry-breach if missing > 30s, but surface as ‘telemetry blackout’ and wait 30s before auto-action.
- Q: How to handle concurrent schedule edits by multiple operators? Proposal: optimistic locking with clear changelog and a ‘You are editing stale draft’ banner; require merge or force-apply.
- Q: Can fallback be chained? e.g., fallback to safe-model then to region. Proposal: allow single-level fallback only for MVP, chain in v2.
- Q: How to compute estimated impact for multi-variant A/B experiments where traffic is split non-sequentially? Proposal: show per-variant expected absolute requests/sec and relative ratio to baseline.

Acceptance criteria (for an MVP ticket):
- UI to create a 3-step percent schedule and persist to rollout-scheduler API (end-to-end).
- Attach a single guardrail (p95 > threshold) and configure fallback to control. If p95 breaches, scheduler triggers fallback and UI shows rollback event.
- Timeline shows telemetry ribbons (p95) for variants and allows hover-scrub revealing metric snapshot.
- Audit trail entry is created for start/pause/abort actions with operator identity.

Prototype links / quick refs:
- Figma frame (draft): https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE/percentile-scheduler-mvp (placeholder)
- Backend API spec: CONFLUENCE-1234#api-scheduler
- Related Jira: JIRA-9876, JIRA-9901 (telemetry tagging)

Open next steps (who/when):
- Product (Sofia) to convert acceptance criteria into 2-week sprint epic (by 2025-03-05).
- Eng (Arjun) to confirm backend schedule API fields and whether step mutation during live ramp is allowed (by 2025-02-22).
- Observability (Maeve) to prototype 10s sparkline panel and telemetry ribbon color thresholds (by 2025-02-28).
- SRE (Diego) to surface recommended guardrail defaults (p95 per-route baselines) and testing plan for blackout behaviour (by 2025-03-04).

Notes to self / loose thoughts (stream-of-consciousness):
- Keep the timeline compact — operators want to quickly see if any step is risky. Maybe collapse step rows by default and show only the current + next step.
- Consider a keyboard-first quick-start (type ‘/rollout create’ in the console) for power users.
- Need to reconcile cost-estimate noise for high-variance token workloads — show range not single number.
- For A/B tests, we might want a different visual (parallel lane view) vs. sequential percent ramp; avoid mixing the two visuals in the same screen unless there’s an explicit mode toggle.

If anyone reading: please add comments inline in the Figma or leave notes here. I want to lock down the core interactions before exploratory visuals are polished.
